claim: Exponential decay: one RK4 step multiplies the amount by R(z) = 1 + z + z²/2 + z³/6 + z⁴/24 with z = −k·Δt, N steps by R(z)^N, and N steps land within N·|z|⁵/120·R(z)^(N−1) of the exact x₀·e^(−kt).
derivation: dx/dt = −k·x with k = 0.5 per hour, Δt = 0.1 hour and x₀ = 1000 molecules: f is linear, with λ = −k, so z = λ·Δt = −0.05 (MODEL.md E3).
The initial value is the parameter x₀ itself, so x = 1000 exactly at step 0 (E5).
So x after n steps is 1000·R(z)^n: 951.2294270833333 after 1 step, 606.5306761801415 after 10 and 367.87946114753964 after 20, computed with exact fractions and rounded once.

Floating point follows these only up to rounding: about ten roundings a step, each within 1.1e-16 of a value below 1000, so within about 1e-12 after one step (tolerance 1e-10) and 2.2e-11 after 20 (tolerance 1e-9). Both are four orders of magnitude below RK4's distance from the exact solution, so they pin the arithmetic to E3.
The exact solution is x₀·e^(−kt): 606.5306597126335 at t = 1 hour (10 steps) and 367.87944117144233 at t = 2 hours (20 steps).
e^z − R(z) = z⁵/5! + z⁶/6! + …, an alternating series of shrinking terms for |z| < 6, so |e^z − R(z)| ≤ |z|⁵/120 = 2.604e-9, and R(z) > e^z > 0.

|a^N − b^N| ≤ N·|a − b|·max(a, b)^(N−1) for a, b > 0, so |x₀R^N − x₀e^(Nz)| ≤ x₀·N·|z|⁵/120·R^(N−1): 1.6605e-5 at N = 10 (R⁹ = 0.63763) and 2.0143e-5 at N = 20 (R¹⁹ = 0.38674). The tolerances, 1.67e-5 and 2.02e-5, are those bounds rounded up; the room left over is far more than rounding needs.
Calculator check with exact fractions: x₀R^N − x₀e^(Nz) = 1.6468e-5 at N = 10 and 1.9976e-5 at N = 20, inside the bounds.

anchors.need: None: a hand-built oracle model, taken from no paper.
